title: How Your Phone Knows Where You Are: GPS in 75 Seconds

scenes.title: The Blue Dot's Secret
scenes.purpose: Hook the viewer with the everyday blue dot and the surprising distance to the satellites behind it.
scenes.narration: A blue dot on your map knows where you are, often within a few meters. Its secret? Satellites about twenty thousand kilometers overhead.

scenes.title: Thirty Satellites, Atomic Clocks
scenes.purpose: Introduce the constellation and the very precise clocks each satellite carries.
scenes.narration: About thirty GPS satellites circle the Earth. Each one carries atomic clocks, accurate to a few billionths of a second.

scenes.title: Your Phone Only Listens
scenes.purpose: Explain what the signal carries and that the receiver is passive, correcting the 'phone pings satellites' myth.
scenes.narration: Each satellite keeps broadcasting two things: where it is, and the exact time. Your phone only listens. It never sends anything back.

scenes.title: Time Becomes Distance
scenes.purpose: Show how travel time multiplied by the speed of light gives the distance to each satellite.
scenes.narration: Your phone compares when each signal left with when it arrived. That's under a tenth of a second. Multiply that time by the speed of light, and you get the distance.

scenes.title: Circles That Cross
scenes.purpose: Demonstrate trilateration with overlapping circles on a flat map, then extend the idea to spheres in 3D.
scenes.narration: One distance puts you somewhere on a circle. Two circles cross at two points. A third crosses only one of them. That's you. In real space, they're spheres, but it works the same way.

scenes.title: Why Four Satellites
scenes.purpose: Explain that the phone's cheap clock adds a shared error, and a fourth satellite lets it solve for that error.
scenes.narration: So why four satellites? Your phone's clock is cheap. Just a millionth of a second off puts you about three hundred meters wrong. But every distance is off equally. A fourth satellite lets the phone fix its clock until the spheres meet.

scenes.title: Back to the Blue Dot
scenes.purpose: Tie the process back to the moving blue dot and give a one-line recap.
scenes.narration: Your phone repeats this nonstop, so the blue dot follows you. So remember: satellites send the time, time becomes distance, and four distances find you.
